exposure: Maternal age group (<25 years, 25-35 years, >35 years)
outcome: Mode of delivery (Vaginal Birth After Cesarean (VBAC), Trial of Labor After Cesarean (TOLAC), repeat Cesarean Delivery (CD))
cohort: The study included 2,729 women in their second pregnancies with a prior cesarean delivery.
finding: Maternal age is an important predictor of repeat cesarean, with younger mothers (under 25 years) having a significantly higher chance of successful VBAC compared to older mothers (over 35 years).
mod_finding: Maternal age emerged as an important predictor of repeat cesarean, with younger mothers having a much higher chance of successful VBAC (47.3% in YG vs 22.8% in AG among those who opted for TOLAC).
